phys_3_4 G4.issue: KICD outcome (d) 'functions of the parts of an electroscope' was never taught, and no low-cost electroscope was offered; both added in Lesson 8 (and parts named earlier, in Lesson 5). KICD outcome (d) asks learners to explain the functions of the parts of an electroscope; the lessons used the electroscope from Lesson 5 but never said what the parts do. Teacher decision: the list of parts and functions follows a standard gold-leaf electroscope, but a teacher should confirm it matches the apparatus in their school. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL Hold up the electroscope and point out the cap, metal stem and leaf, and say what each part does: the metal cap collects charge, the metal stem and leaf are conductors so the charge spreads along them, the light leaf is free to swing away from the stem, and the insulating stopper and the case stop charge leaking away and draughts moving the leaf. Ask learners to say each function back in their own words.

phys_3_4 G6.issue: Lesson 8 was listed as '40 minutes (or 80)'; it needs 80, so it is now a double period. Unit total corrected to 680 minutes (was wrongly 9 x 40 = 360), and over-full lessons 2, 5, 6 and 9 now have minute-by-minute plans. Lesson 8 has a six-step group practical, a demonstration, a particle model, the Driving Question Board and a model revision: far more than 40 minutes. Two options existed (keep 40 and cut, or make it 80); I chose 80 because the electroscope practical is the evidence base for the sign test. The teacher must confirm the school can timetable a double period. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL 80 minutes (2 x 40-minute periods)

phys_3_4 G7.issue: Added language and access supports (Kiswahili key words, choice of ways to show understanding, large-print angle scale); none existed before. The unit had no supports for English learners or learners with special needs. The Kiswahili terms are from general knowledge and have NOT been verified: the teacher must confirm each word matches what is used in local classrooms and replace any that differ. CLAUDE'S PROPOSAL as a question for Lesson 3. Language support: write each key word in English with a Kiswahili support beside it and keep the list displayed (for example electric charge - chaji ya umeme; atom - atomu; electron - elektroni; proton - protoni; neutron - nyutroni; attract - kuvutana; repel - kusukumana; conductor - kondakta; insulator - kihami). Invite learners to correct the list or add words they use at home.
